newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong blue chips end weak, China shares jump.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong blue chips end weak, China shares jump.

text.p: Hong Kong's blue chips closed lower on Monday amid caution ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Senate testimony this week and the political situation in Beijing, but China-related shares jumped.
The Hang Seng Index fell 69.16 points, or 0.51 percent, to 13,375.69. Turnover was HK$8.80 billion compared with HK$8.21 billion on Friday.
"For the past few trading days the uptrend has been quite strong and quite overdone so it is just a correction," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
"Political stability is still unclear in Beijing so there is some uncertainty," he added.
Analysts said that while the death of Deng Xiaoping had cleared uncertainty in the market, investors would continue to watch developments in Beijing.
"I think in the near term people will look at whether there is any major reshuffling of the political line," said Edward Chan, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
He said investors were also refocusing on fundamentals and would pay close attention to Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
"He will mainly talk about the inflationary picture and GDP growth. I think the market would like to see how he builds the overall picture," said Chan.
Shares in China-related stocks moved ahead in active trade on Monday. Brokers said covered warrants on a basket of red chips was planned.
The H-share index of mainland Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong surged 25.74 points, or 2.71 percent, to 973.91, with constituent China Eastern Airlines soaring HK$0.22 to HK$1.63.
Red chip favourite Shanghai Industrial gained HK$1.30 to HK$33.00 and CITIC Pacific rose HK$0.80 to HK$39.40.
"After a consolidation, the shares are picking up," said Boby Ho, dealing manager at GK Goh Securities.
Shares in Television Broadcasts ended unchanged at HK$34.00. Shaw Brothers and The Shaw Foundation bought Pearson Plc's 10 percent stake in the company. Shaw Brothers shares fell HK$0.40 to HK$8.70.
